note: Adapted from Light & Wilson 1936, original in English (The nasute termites of the Philippines, The Philippine Journal of Science 60: 461–520). Both the alate and the worker are given as Unknown in the original; type collection No. 1131, Cotabato Province, Mindanao; the species appears twenty times in the collection records, distributed from Ilocos Norte, Luzon, to Sir J. Brooke Point in southern Palawan and to Cotabato, Mindanao, and especially abundant on the slopes of Mariveles and Maquiling. Fig. 9 (soldier head in dorsal and lateral view, left mandible) not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The only Philippine nasute termite whose soldier has a yellow head and a conical nasus; closest to N. javanicus (Holmgren), but distinctly larger.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Posterior part of the head smoky yellowish brown, darker at the sides and in front; base of the nasus burnt umber, apex pale red; abdominal tergites pale smoky brown; sternites pale yellow with a faint smoky tinge; the rest pale white-yellow. Head and nasus shape as in Fig. 9 a, b; outline in dorsal view distinctly convex, concave at the base of the nasus owing to a slight constriction. Head densely covered with long fine white hairs. Antennae 11-segmented, about two thirds as long as head plus nasus. Measurements (mm and indices, from type collection No. 1131, three typical soldiers from Cotabato Province, Mindanao): head plus nasus 1.23, 1.23, 1.29; head length (excluding nasus) 0.78, 0.75, 0.81; nasus length 0.45, 0.48, 0.48; head projection 0.22, 0.22, 0.24; head height 0.45, 0.43, 0.51; head width 0.74, 0.72, 0.81; fore tibia length 0.54, 0.48, 0.54; head index 0.95, 0.96, 1.00; head-nasus index 0.65, 0.71, 0.70; head projection index 0.29, 0.33, 0.29; leg extension index 0.83, 0.76.
